definitions.gloss: autumn equinox period; autumn higan; autumn week of Buddhist memorial services
definitions.explanation: A seven-day period centered on the autumn equinox (around September 22-23), during which Japanese families visit ancestral graves and make offerings. The autumn counterpart of {春彼岸|はるひがん}.

examples.japanese: {秋彼岸|あきひがん}にはお{墓|はか}を{掃除|そうじ}する。
examples.english: I clean the graves during the autumn equinox period.

examples.japanese: {秋彼岸|あきひがん}にはおはぎをお{供|そな}えするのが{伝統|でんとう}だ。
examples.english: It's traditional to offer ohagi during the autumn equinox period.

examples.japanese: {秋彼岸|あきひがん}を{過|す}ぎると{朝晩|あさばん}はぐっと{涼|すず}しくなり、{秋|あき}の{深|ふか}まりを{感|かん}じる。
examples.english: After the autumn equinox period passes, mornings and evenings become noticeably cooler, and you can feel autumn deepening.

notes:
Compound of {秋|あき} ('autumn') and {彼岸|ひがん} ('equinox period'). The autumn counterpart of {春彼岸|はるひがん}, with the same structure of grave visits and offerings but associated with different seasonal imagery.

CULTURAL NOTE:
- Like spring higan, spans seven days: three before, the equinox day, and three after
- The traditional offering is {御萩|おはぎ} (ohagi), a rice ball coated in red bean paste, named after the autumn bush clover ({萩|はぎ})
- {彼岸花|ひがんばな} (red spider lily) blooms around this time and is closely associated with the period
- The proverb {暑|あつ}さ{寒|さむ}さも{彼岸|ひがん}まで ('heat and cold last until higan') marks this as a seasonal turning point

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {秋彼岸|あきひがん}のお{墓参|はかまい}り: autumn equinox grave visit
- {秋彼岸|あきひがん}の{入|い}り: start of the autumn higan period
- {秋彼岸|あきひがん}の{中日|ちゅうにち}: the middle day (equinox itself)
- {秋彼岸|あきひがん}の{明|あ}け: end of the autumn higan period

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {春彼岸|はるひがん}: spring equinox period — the same observance around the spring equinox in March
- {彼岸|ひがん}: equinox period (general) — can refer to either spring or autumn higan
- お{盆|ぼん}: Obon; Bon festival — another major ancestor memorial period in mid-August
